title: Fleet Command: Orchestrating Edge AI
description: NVIDIA Fleet Command is the enterprise platform for deploying, managing, and updating AI applications across fleets of edge servers — one console for hundreds of distant machines. The EGX platform is the underlying edge-AI hardware/software stack it manages. Together they are the control plane for distributed AI.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: EGX Platform: The Edge Stack
description: NVIDIA EGX combines edge GPUs, networking, and the AI software stack into deployable edge systems — the hardware Fleet Command orchestrates. From Jetson-class devices to EGX servers, the stack scales. The platform is the fleet's body; Fleet Command is its nervous system.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: OTA Updates: Staged Rollouts
description: Fleet Command pushes over-the-air updates to edge nodes in staged waves — canary, ring, fleet — with health gates between waves. A bad update stops at the canary instead of bricking the fleet. Staging is how you update what you cannot visit.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Zero-Touch Provisioning
description: New edge nodes provision zero-touch: unbox, network-boot or image, and the node enrolls, attests, and pulls its workload assignment. Fleets scale by shipping boxes. The console does the rest.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Application Deployment at Scale
description: AI applications deploy as versioned packages across the fleet — same model, same config, everywhere, or per-site variants where needed. Rollback is a version change. Consistency across distance is the product.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Fleet Health Monitoring
description: Fleet Command watches node health — GPU temps, disk, network, application metrics — with alerts on drift and failure. A thousand nodes need a single pane of glass. Monitoring is how the fleet tells you it needs help.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Security: Attested Edge Nodes
description: Edge nodes attest their boot state before joining work — measured boot plus Fleet Command verification, so compromised nodes do not get workloads. Keys rotate, access is role-based. The edge is hostile territory; admission is earned.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Offline and Intermittent Operation
description: Edge nodes must work through disconnected stretches — cached models, local inference, queued telemetry that syncs when the link returns. Fleet Command designs for intermittent, not just remote. Disconnected is a mode, not a failure.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Model Version Management
description: Fleet Command versions models like code — A/B tests, canary models, instant rollback — because models are software with weights. Serving the wrong model version is a production incident. Version discipline applies to weights too.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Multi-Tenancy on Edge Nodes
description: Edge nodes isolate tenants — containers, GPU slices, network policies — so shared infrastructure does not mean shared data. Quotas keep one tenant from starving others. The edge is shared; the isolation is real.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Bandwidth-Efficient Sync
description: Fleet links are thin: Fleet Command syncs deltas, compresses models, and schedules transfers off-peak. Every byte across the edge link is budgeted. Efficiency is respect for the constraint.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Disaster Recovery for Fleets
description: Fleet configurations back up centrally — node definitions, app versions, policies — so a dead site rebuilds from the console's memory. Recovery is re-provisioning, not archaeology. The fleet's memory lives off the edge.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Compliance and Audit Trails
description: Fleet Command logs who deployed what where — the audit trail for regulated edge AI. Compliance reports generate from the same data as operations. Regulated fleets prove their state on demand.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: Capacity Planning
description: Fleet growth gets planned — GPU headroom, link budgets, power and cooling at sites — before the queue backs up. Utilization trends trigger procurement. Planning beats panic.
provenance: Public record: compiled from official project documentation and published specifications. Fact-checked 2026-10-21.

title: The Fleet Operations Picture
description: Ladder-top Fleet Command: attested nodes, staged updates, versioned models, watched health, audited everything. Fifteen rungs from one edge server to a centrally-run distributed AI fleet.
